analysis:
Integrated all four supplied analyses and checked the available replayed source directly. No independently supported security regression is established. The provider build action defaults save-caches to false and explicitly gates Swift, SwiftPM and Metal cache writes (.github/actions/provider-ci-build/action.yml head:7–9,107,116,143). SwiftPM restore keys include OS, workspace/home layout, lane and lockfile identity (head:42–53). These CI caches are distinct from consumer KV storage under T-041; no visible change alters prompt encryption, tenant isolation, authorization, attestation or billing.

The reported .git caching raises an artifact-integrity contract relevant to A-011/A-017 and T-013/T-054: connectivity checks do not authenticate configuration, hooks or producers. However, an adversarial writer to a cache consumed by trusted jobs is not established, so poisoning is not a finding. Replay omits the ci.yml checkout/save implementations and much of the workflow tests; their push-only write policy and restore provenance cannot be independently reconciled here.

component-changes.yml:12–13,28,39 forwards mimo_audio from scripts/ci-component-paths.py, but that classifier and the consuming ci.yml gate are not replayed. Review must confirm complete gate-input coverage and unconditional master-push execution before accepting the narrower audio test policy claimed in changelog.d/ci-git-swiftpm-cache.md:8. docs-impact.yml:59–68 retains full history while excluding evidence archives and landing media; its signature check remains separate and unchanged.

Remaining material review: actual ci.yml cache scopes/write gates, changed classifier behavior, source/build-cache invalidation and tool-cache provenance. Missing implementations and incomplete replay are coverage limits, not evidence of vulnerabilities or safety.
